hints: Focus on what hot concentrated sulfuric acid does to an alcohol, think elimination rather than oxidation or substitution.
Menthol is a secondary cyclic alcohol, so removing the $\text{-OH}$ group plus a hydrogen from a neighbouring ring carbon will create a $\text{C=C}$ inside the ring.
Two ring alkenes are possible, so compare their substitution to pick the more stable, more substituted Zaitsev major product.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the reaction type**

Heating an alcohol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ causes acid-catalysed dehydration, loss of water to form an alkene.

$$\text{R-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{-R'} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4, \text{ heat}} \text{R-CH=CH-R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find where the double bond can form**

In menthol the $\text{-OH}$ is on a ring carbon with two different ring neighbours, one bearing a $\text{-CH}_3$ group and one bearing a $\text{-CH(CH}_3)_2$ group. Removing $\text{-OH}$ plus $\text{H}$ from either neighbour gives a $\text{C=C}$ in the ring, not outside it and not a $\text{C=O}$.

**Apply Zaitsev to choose the major alkene**

Both possible alkenes are trisubstituted, but the alkene with the double bond next to the isopropyl group has more alkyl character and more hyperconjugative $\text{C-H}$ bonds, so it is slightly more stable. That is the major product T, with the $\text{C=C}$ between the original $\text{C-OH}$ carbon and the $\text{C-isopropyl}$ carbon.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows an exocyclic $\text{C=C}$ on the isopropyl side chain. Dehydration removes $\text{H}$ from a ring carbon directly attached to $\text{C-OH}$, it does not create a double bond outside the ring without rearrangement.
options.B: Incorrect. This is a ketone formed by oxidation of a secondary alcohol. Hot concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ acts here as a dehydrating agent to give an alkene, not as an oxidant like acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$.
options.C: Incorrect. This is a possible dehydration product with $\text{C=C}$ between the methyl-bearing carbon and the original $\text{C-OH}$ carbon, but it is the less stable minor alkene. It has fewer hyperconjugative hydrogens than the isopropyl-substituted isomer.
options.D: Correct. This is the major Zaitsev dehydration product. Loss of $\text{-OH}$ plus $\text{H}$ from the isopropyl-bearing neighbour gives the more substituted, more stable ring alkene with $\text{C=C}$ between C2 and C3 of the menthol skeleton.
